title: QW-Ratio Scaffolded 22-Layer Stack with Differential Evolution
scientific_hypothesis: A deterministic quarter-wave ratio scaffold (t_TiO2/t_SiO2 = 0.60) initialized from the best-performing candidate thicknesses will preserve phase coherence while differential evolution searches for optimal absolute thickness offsets, achieving target scores ≥0.90 without topology drift.
design_principle: Quarter-wave baseline initialization with fixed odd/even thickness ratio provides physically motivated starting point; differential evolution with population=40, F=0.9, CR=0.85 explores configuration space while layer-count locking prevents accidental topology swaps.
proposed_topology: 22-layer alternating stack: Air | (TiO2|SiO2)_11 | Fused Silica substrate. Layer 1 (odd) = TiO2, Layer 2 (even) = SiO2, continuing alternation through Layer 22.
design_variables: absolute thickness offsets for all 22 layers with t_odd/t_even ratio anchored at 0.60 ± 0.05 nm tolerance
manufacturing_considerations: absolute thickness tolerance ±5 nm for robustness analysis
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack initialization is standard for dielectric multilayer designs requiring broadband reflection
Differential evolution preserves population diversity for multi-modal optimization landscapes
expected_advantages: Phase coherence preserved through ratio scaffolding
Global search capability of differential evolution avoids local minima
Layer-count locking prevents topology drift during mutation
known_risks: Ratio constraint may limit search space if optimal design requires different odd/even proportions
Differential evolution computational cost scales with population size
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer alternating TiO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate at 45 degrees incidence. Initialize with quarter-wave ratio scaffold where t_TiO2/t_SiO2 = 0.60 anchored to the best-performing candidate thicknesses from prior iteration (Layer 2 SiO2 thickness as reference). Apply differential evolution optimizer with population size 40, mutation factor F=0.9, crossover rate CR=0.85. Enforce strict layer-count locking to prevent topology changes during mutation. Evaluate reflectance in 450-650 nm band and transmittance in 700-1000 nm band. Include ±5 nm absolute thickness tolerance for robustness scoring. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 450-650 nm, 700-1000 nm. soft objectives: high reflectance in 450-650 nm; high transmittance in 700-1000 nm; minimized crosstalk between bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 450-650 nm; reflectance in 700-1000 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 24 layers.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: QW ratio scaffold (0.60), differential evolution optimizer, layer-count locking. Differs from iteration_07 by explicit ratio constraint and DE optimizer instead of gradient_thickness.
